title: Mark Topics Known
bottom_line: Run /explain:explain-known with topic names, or with nothing to use your IDE selection or project, so explanations stop explaining what you already know.

sections.heading: You need only Claude Code, plus an optional IDE

cards.title: git (optional)
cards.text: Used, when present, to name the current project after its repository.

cards.title: A connected IDE (optional)
cards.text: Without an argument, the skills use the code highlighted in the IDE, or the opened file. With no IDE connected, they fall back to the current project.

blocks.title: First use
blocks.text: If your profile at `~/.explain_skill/profile.md` does not exist yet, Claude first asks the two first-use questions of the explain skill: which topics you want to learn, and which you already know well. It writes the profile, then continues.

blocks.title: Settings
blocks.text: None. The plugin has no environment variables and no plugin settings. It runs only when you type it; Claude never starts it on its own.

terms.definition: The code editor connected to Claude Code, which tells Claude which lines you selected and which file you opened.
A language, framework, tool or project, such as Go, .NET or your codebase.
The topics you know well. Explanations may assume them.
The topics you are learning. Explanations define their concepts before using them.
Plain Markdown notes in `~/.explain_skill/` recording which concepts you have covered.

sections.heading: What you type decides what gets marked known

blocks.title: The command
blocks.code: /explain:explain-known [topic, topic, ...]  (empty = IDE selection, then opened file, then current project)

blocks.title: Three ways to use it
blocks.caption: With an IDE, the highlighted code is used first, then the opened file if nothing is highlighted.

blocks.title: Examples
blocks.code:
/explain:explain-known C++, Python
/explain:explain-known            # I understand the highlighted code (or, without an IDE: I know this codebase)

sections.heading: Topic names move whole topics to your known list

steps.title: Your list is split on commas
steps.text: For example `C++, Python` becomes two topics.

steps.title: Each topic leaves the learning list
steps.text: If it is listed there. Matching ignores case and treats aliases as the same topic (`golang` = Go, `dotnet` = .NET). Project entries keep their " (project)" suffix.

steps.title: Each topic joins the known list
Its notes are kept
steps.text: If you later move the topic back to learning, the log is still there.

sections.heading: With no argument, it logs the code you understand

before.label: What you mean
before.text: "I understand this code": the highlighted lines, or the whole opened file if nothing is highlighted.

after.label: What changes
after.text: The concepts that code uses are logged as understood. The language itself stays on the learning list.

blocks.title: What happens
items: Claude reads the target: the selected lines, or the whole opened file if nothing is selected.

It lists the concepts the target uses, grouped by topic. For an opened file, it also notes the file's role in the project (the component, what it does, and how it connects to other modules) under the project topic.
Only concepts that belong to a topic on your learning list are logged. Concepts from known topics are skipped.
Each remaining concept is logged as understood at depth "core", with a history note "<date>, from <path:lines>: marked known by the user".
If a concept is already logged, only that history note is added, and its depth is raised only if it was "surface".

sections.heading: With no argument and no IDE, your project becomes known

nodes.label: Current project name
nodes.note: The git repository name, or the folder name.

blocks.caption: The same steps as for topic names are applied to the project's name.

blocks.title: Defaults this changes
rows: The current project (its git repo name) is registered as a topic you are learning
`/explain:explain-known` with no argument and no IDE marks it known
Explanations go only as deep as your known topics and the log allow
The learning log lives in `~/.explain_skill/`, shared by every project on the machine
Not configurable; edit or delete the files by hand

sections.heading: A short reply tells you what changed

cards.title: The target it used
cards.text: A topic, a selection, a file, or the project.

cards.title: What it added or moved
cards.text: The topics or concepts now treated as known.

blocks.caption: Claude replies in one short message with these three things.

next_action.text: Run `/explain:explain-known` followed by the languages you know well, such as `C++, Python`.
next_action.detail: Explanations may then assume those topics without explaining them.
